name: Cameron Winter
label: Partisan
lede: Cameron Winter quit hockey after concussions, took up the piano, and made a baritone record his own label doubted could pay his rent. Pitchfork put it third on its 2025 albums list.

eras.title: A hockey kid, a basement in Fort Greene
eras.text: Winter grew up in Park Slope, lost hockey to concussions and found songs instead. By 2016 he was singing and writing for Geese, a high-school band that rehearsed in a friend's basement.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cameron Winter · NME: Cameron Winter interview
years.h: A twelve-year-old wins the National Math Museum's Pi Day song contest
years.p: Cameron Winter's father, the composer Stewart Winter, put the winning entry on SoundCloud, where it still sits.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports that Winter played competitive youth ice hockey until concussions ended it, and that music took over from there. The Pi Day entry is the earliest thing of his that's still online.

Winter has since said the head injuries left him with what he calls a traumatic childhood, in an NME interview around the release of his debut album.

years.h: Geese form at two Brooklyn schools and rehearse in Max Bassin's basement
years.p: Winter sang and played keys and wrote most of the songs for [[Geese|e0c97a4d-c392-41a9-a374-57af3e3eeab3]], which started in 2016 with students from Brooklyn Friends and Little Red School House.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, the band rehearsed and recorded in drummer Max Bassin's basement in Fort Greene. The name came from guitarist Emily Green's nickname, Goose. Their first song together was a cover of Tame Impala's "Mind Mischief".

Winter applied to Boston University for communications, then skipped college for the band. This page follows his solo work; Geese has its own.

years.h: Winter and Oliver Seda self-release Elephant Hunter as Men of the Reef
years.p: The duo's EP came out a year before Geese signed to Partisan.

eras.title: A label deal, then a long stay in Tuxedo
eras.text: Label interest arrived in the pandemic summer of 2020. By 2023 Winter was writing songs that didn't fit Geese, and he took them to the one engineer he knew.

years.h: Geese meant to quit after high school; labels called instead
years.p: Self-produced demos drew label interest in mid-2020, and the deal that later released Winter's solo work followed.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the signing to 2020, after the demos attracted interest that mid-year. Partisan and Play It Again Sam would release both [[Geese|e0c97a4d-c392-41a9-a374-57af3e3eeab3]]'s records and everything Winter did alone.

years.src: Wikipedia: Heavy Metal (album) · NME: Cameron Winter interview
years.h: Four months of sessions in Tuxedo stretch to a year and a half
years.p: Winter started Heavy Metal in July at Loren Humphrey's studio, in an estate guest house in Tuxedo, NY, on a four-month plan. By his own account it ran closer to eighteen months.
years.xp:
Loren Humphrey, who'd worked on Geese's 3D Country that year, engineered and mixed with Winter. Winter picked him, according to Wikipedia, because he was the only engineer he knew personally. Extra sessions happened at Diamond Mine in Long Island City and in Winter's childhood bedroom.

He played most of the instruments himself. Guests included James Richardson on classical guitar, trumpet and French horn, plus Jesse Kontansky on violin, Xan Aird on guitar and Peter Hess on sax and clarinet. Winter told NME the project was disruptive to Geese's schedule, though the band backed him.

eras.title: The label doubts it, the internet doesn't
eras.text: Partisan wasn't sure a record this odd could sell, so it went out in December with two teasers and a stream of tall tales from the artist.

years.h: Winter's first solo release is two songs, one written at sixteen
years.p: Singles puts out "Vines" and "Take It With You", both written and produced by Winter.
years.xp:
Winter has said "Vines" is the song that got him his record deal, according to Wikipedia. His label later asked him to swap it for a different track on Heavy Metal, and he refused.

Stereogum's Danielle Chelosky heard Leonard Cohen in the writing; NME read "Vines" as a young man's self-reckoning.

years.cap: Winter at Joe's Pub, New York
years.h: "$0" goes up as a free download, and the tall tales begin
years.p: Winter posted "$0" on his own site on November 13 and the album was announced November 19. He told interviewers he'd hired musicians off Craigslist and a five-year-old bassist.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the rollout jokes as unsubstantiated: Craigslist players, a five-year-old on bass, sessions at several Guitar Center stores. In reality the record is mostly Winter and Humphrey.

q: I'm young and not afraid of living with my parents.
years.src: Wikipedia: Heavy Metal (album) · NME: Cameron Winter interview
years.h: Partisan puts Heavy Metal out into the quiet of December
years.p: Winter's debut solo album opens with "The Rolling Stones" and closes with "Can't Keep Anything", ten songs in 43 minutes.
years.xp:
Partisan founder Tim Putnam told Winter, as Wikipedia relays it, that the record wasn't commercial enough to get him out of his parents' house. Winter answered in public.

The label cut and reworked tracks, then still held it for the quiet December release window. He found the title in a line of "Cancer of the Skull" and thought it "a funny title", he told NME.

eras.title: The year everybody caught up
eras.text: The record Partisan hedged on kept climbing. By December Winter was headlining rooms built for orchestras, and Pitchfork had his song at No. 1.

yt: Love Takes Miles, Later... with Jools Holland
years.h: Winter plays "Love Takes Miles" on Later... with Jools Holland
years.p: The BBC show gave him his biggest television slot to date, alone at a piano.

years.h: Geese put out Getting Killed in the middle of his solo run
years.p: The band's third album for Partisan landed the same year as his solo record, and Rolling Stone UK called Winter a defining Gen Z figure. See [[Geese|e0c97a4d-c392-41a9-a374-57af3e3eeab3]].

years.big: "a project of catharsis that never comes across like an exercise in vanity"
years.src: Wikipedia: Heavy Metal (album) · Album of the Year · RGM
years.h: Pitchfork ranks Heavy Metal third for 2025 and "Love Takes Miles" first
years.p: Walden Green wrote that line in Pitchfork's review, which gave the album 8.3 and Best New Music. "Love Takes Miles" was named song of the year on December 1.
years.xp:
Green called Winter's voice a woozy baritone. Album of the Year lists the score as 83 out of 100.

Elsewhere, Wikipedia records the album at No. 4 for Rough Trade, No. 14 for Consequence and No. 32 for Rolling Stone; Nick Cave called the record startling, per the same page. Pitchfork's review text was not fetched directly; the quote and score come from Wikipedia's reception table and Album of the Year.

q: Is this enough for you people?!
years.src: Rolling Stone UK: Cameron Winter live in London
yt: Nina + Field of Cops, Paris, Dec 3
years.h: A Steinway at the Roundhouse, and half the room looking at his back
years.p: Winter played 13 songs from Heavy Metal alone. When a fan shouted "Turn around!", he repositioned and asked if that was enough.
years.xp: Rolling Stone UK reviewed the show and noted he played final notes so quietly it read as a refusal to become a rock cliche. The next night he played Cabaret Sauvage in Paris.

years.cap: Winter at Carnegie Hall, New York, December 2025
years.src: Paste: Carnegie Hall · Wikipedia: Love Takes Miles
years.h: Winter headlines Carnegie Hall at 23 while Paul Thomas Anderson films
years.p: Anderson and Benny Safdie shot the sold-out Stern Auditorium show on Panavision 35mm, from the stage and the balcony.
years.xp: Paste reported the crowd included Joe Keery, Lucas Hedges and Trey Anastasio, and that the filming was not officially explained that night. Hedges had already starred in the December 2025 video for "Love Takes Miles".

eras.title: Carnegie Hall becomes a movie and a record
eras.text: The Carnegie Hall night turned into a film and a live album, and Winter was already road-testing songs the studio record never had.

years.cap: Cameron Winter solo at Joe's Pub, New York
years.src: Wikipedia: Live at Carnegie Hall · Rolling Stone Australia
years.h: Live at Carnegie Hall comes out with three new songs
years.p: Due October 9 on Partisan and Play It Again Sam, it holds nine songs from Singles and Heavy Metal plus three unreleased ones, including "It All Fell in the River".
years.xp:
Anderson's Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall premieres at the New York Film Festival on October 1, with Janus Films releasing it in North America on November 20, 2026, and Mubi handling the rest of the world in 2027. Wikipedia says all screenings are on 35mm.

Winter had been road-testing unreleased songs such as "Emperor XIII in Shades" and "Ben" at a solo cathedral show in Auckland on February 4, per Rolling Stone Australia.
